Definition: something sown (only in the plural), i.e. a vegetable (as food)
BiblicalUsage: Pulse — the vegetables sown for food — is what this word means, and it appears twice, both times in Daniel's test. Daniel asks for pulse and water instead of the king's meat, and after ten days he and his friends look better than the rest. The plain food of the field becomes the proof of God's care.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Daniel's pulse is a quiet kind of faith: obeying God in small choices and trusting Him with the outcome.
